prompt: The loyalty team gives a registered customer gold status on the order that takes the customer's spend in the first half of 2025 to 4,000 euros or more. Use the orders with a customer_id (guest orders have a missing customer_id) whose order_ts, a moment in UTC, is from 1 January 2025 00:00 up to but not including 1 July 2025 00:00. An order's value is the total net_revenue_eur of its lines in sales. Add up each customer's order values one order at a time, in order of order_ts. Orders of a customer that tie on order_ts are added one at a time too: the order with the lower order_id comes first. For each customer whose running spend reaches 4,000 or more, return four columns, in this order: customer_id; order_id, the order on which the running spend first reached 4,000 or more; gold_date, the UTC date of that order's order_ts; and spend_to_date_eur, the running spend up to and including that order. Leave out the customers who never reach 4,000. Sort by customer_id from low to high.
hints: Next, write each order's value, then each customer's running spend in order of order_ts and order_id.
Write the frame out so orders with the same order_ts get running totals of their own, then keep the order whose running spend reaches 4,000 while the spend before it was below 4,000.
why_this_works: A ROWS frame ordered by order_ts and then order_id adds tied orders one at a time, and the crossing order is the one whose spend before it was still below 4,000.
